# hostd_vm_firewall (Resource)

The firewall of one VM: whether it is enabled, the default policies, and the ordered rules and attached security groups. The firewall filters the public interface. Use one `hostd_vm_firewall` per VM; `rules` is the complete list, so rules added outside Terraform are removed on the next apply. Rules are written before the options, so enabling the firewall with `policy_in = "DROP"` does not cut off traffic the rules allow. Destroy removes every rule and turns the firewall off, as on a new VM. Import with `<project_id>,<vmid>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hostd_vm_firewall" "web" {
  project_id = hostd_vm.web.project_id
  vmid       = hostd_vm.web.vmid
  enable     = true
  policy_in  = "DROP"
  policy_out = "ACCEPT"

  # Evaluated top to bottom. Terraform keeps exactly this list on the VM.
  rules = [
    { type = "group", action = hostd_security_group.web.pve_group_name },
    { type = "in", action = "ACCEPT", proto = "icmp", comment = "ping" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the VM firewall is enabled.
- `policy_in` (String) Default policy for inbound traffic: `ACCEPT` or `DROP`.
- `policy_out` (String) Default policy for outbound traffic: `ACCEPT` or `DROP`.
- `project_id` (String) UUID of the project the VM belongs to.
- `vmid` (Number) VM identifier (`hostd_vm.vmid`).

### Optional

- `rules` (Attributes List) Rules and attached security groups in evaluation order. Empty by default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) `ACCEPT` or `DROP` for a packet filter. For `type = "group"`, the security group's `pve_group_name`.
- `type` (String) `in` or `out` for a packet filter, or `group` to attach a security group.

Optional:

- `comment` (String) Free-text comment, up to 255 characters.
- `dest` (String) Destination address, CIDR (IPv4 no larger than `/26`, IPv6 no larger than `/64`), IPv4 range, or an IP set as `+<pve_ipset_name>`. Empty matches any.
- `dport` (String) Destination port, range (`80:85`) or comma-separated list. TCP and UDP only.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to true.
- `proto` (String) `tcp`, `udp` or `icmp` for a packet filter. Leave empty for a security group.
- `source` (String) Source address, CIDR (IPv4 no larger than `/26`, IPv6 no larger than `/64`), IPv4 range, or an IP set as `+<pve_ipset_name>`. Empty matches any.
- `sport` (String) Source port, range (`80:85`) or comma-separated list. TCP and UDP only.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import hostd_vm_firewall.web 0b6e5f7c-4f4e-4a43-9c0e-6f4d3b2a1c90,104
```
